I wanted a drum machine I could open in a tab and start playing straight away - no install, no account, no sample library to download first. So I built BAP Studio. It is 16 velocity-sensitive pads across four banks, a 16-step sequencer with per-step velocity and swing, four patterns that chain into a song, and a sampler that takes any audio file or mic recording, finds the transients and lays the chops across the pads. Every sound is synthesised in the browser, so there is nothing to install and nothing to wait for. You can export a WAV, a MIDI file, or a link that rebuilds your beat exactly as you left it. Quickest way in: press Space to start the loop, then hit Z, C and A. Most people have something going in about a minute. Would love to hear what you make with it.

## Using the drum machine

Click the squares to create your drum beat. Double click the squares to toggle between the hi-hat and open hi-hat, snare drum and cross stick, and high tom-tom and low tom-tom. Click the instrument names on the left to mute the sound.

Click "Settings" to change drum kit, time signature, and activate swing. Click "Beats" to choose common drum beats. You can easily vary the beats by using ride cymbal instead of hi-hat, and cross stick instead of regular snare drum.

# Online drum machine

## What is a drum machine?

A drum machine is an electronic musical instrument that can imitate drum kits and percussion instruments. Some can also produce artificial sound effects. Most drum machines allow users to create their own beats.

A drum machine is commonly used for recording electronic music, often used in house, dance, and hip hop genres. It may also be used as a metronome, as a backing track for practice or as a way to explore a variety of drum rhythms.

### Is this a BandLab alternative?

For beat making specifically, yes. BandLab is a full free online DAW with multi-track recording, virtual instruments, and a social sharing platform — and it's excellent. SoundTools Beat Maker is narrower in scope: a drum machine and step sequencer focused on quickly building and exporting drum patterns. SoundTools requires no account at all, loads instantly, and keeps everything in your browser. If you want to sketch a drum loop fast and export a WAV, SoundTools is quicker to get in and out of. If you want to build a full song, record vocals, and collaborate with others, BandLab is the better platform.

## Related Tools You Might Like [...] Partially. GarageBand (free on Mac and iPhone) is a full music production app with a drum machine, virtual instruments, multi-track recording, and a huge sound library. SoundTools Beat Maker is much more focused — it's a browser-based drum machine and step sequencer, not a full DAW. The advantage: it works on any device including Windows and Android with no download, no account, and no setup. If you want to make a quick drum beat, export it, and get on with your day, SoundTools is faster. If you want to produce a full song with multiple instruments, GarageBand (or BandLab on any device) is the right tool.

### Is this a BandLab alternative? [...] ### Is it really free? What's the catch?

It's 100% free with no limits, no watermarks, no subscriptions, and no hidden charges. Make and export as many beats as you want. Everything processes in your browser — your audio never leaves your device.
